incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code) — Articles L. 223-1 to L. 223-43 (SARL), L. 210-2 (share capital), L. 223-7 (payment-up and escrow of share capital), R. 223-1 et seq., and R. 123-103 (RCS registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce — Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with mandatory electronic filing via the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by INPI.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'une société commerciale (single electronic dossier) submitted on the Guichet Unique portal, accompanied by the Statuts (Articles of Association) and statutory exhibits.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SARL; the capital is freely fixed in the Articles. Where cash contributions are made, at least 20% of the cash capital must be paid up before filing and deposited into a blocked escrow account (séquestre) held by an authorised bank, a notary or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the balance must be paid up within five years (Article L. 223-7 C. com.).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — SARL [NAME]
Adopted at the constitutive meeting on [●].
RESOLVED: (1) The signed Articles of Association are adopted as the constitutional instrument; the share capital of €[●], divided into [●] shares, is confirmed as fully subscribed. (2) The registered office is fixed at [●], France. (3) At least one-fifth of the cash capital has been deposited in a blocked escrow account pursuant to Article L. 223-7 of the French Commercial Code. (4) [Name] is appointed Gérant, with full powers to manage the automated drop-shipping business, open payment accounts (Stripe, PayPal), and complete all registration formalities. (5) All incorporation steps to date are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name availability and business scope check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés via the Infogreffe search portal; INPI trademark database
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Run a negative-name search for the proposed corporate denomination and verify that the planned activity (automated online drop-shipping retail) is compatible with the RCS and statistics classifications. Confirm the territorial jurisdiction of the future registered office and the applicable APE code so that the eventual Guichet Unique dossier is internally consistent.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (dénomination sociale) with three alternates
Statement of the future registered-office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is unavailable or conflicts with an existing trademark or RCS entry, select a new distinctive denomination and re-run the search; amend the corporate object if the competent classification office requests a different APE code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked share-capital escrow and deposit of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved French credit institution, notaire, or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account (séquestre) in the name of the company in formation; transfer the cash contributions subscribed under the Articles, or at least 20% thereof when deferred payment-up is chosen. Obtain from the depositary the 'certificat de dépôt des fonds' (deposit certificate) identifying each contributing shareholder, the amount and the account reference. The funds remain frozen until the RCS issues the Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Valid identity document of each shareholder
Anti-money-laundering and KYC forms of the depositary bank
Bank transfer or cash deposit instruction
Statement of the origin of funds when requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request the bank or notary to rectify the deposit certificate if it contains errors; if the depositary refuses, appoint another authorised credit institution and re-deposit the funds.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - French Public Finances Directorate; official portal: impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a French SARL must first obtain a SIREN number via the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) or the online Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), followed by a SIRET establishment code. For VAT purposes, the entity must apply to the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) having territorial jurisdiction to obtain a French VAT identification number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire). Non-resident entities without a French establishment carrying out taxable transactions in France may register directly with the DGFiP's foreign business unit (Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères). The application requires the foreign entity's statutory documents, proof of identity of legal representatives, and a description of the French taxable activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SARL is by default subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at the entity level. Under Articles 206 and 239 of the French General Tax Code (Code général des impôts), certain closely-held SARLs whose shares are not listed and whose shareholders are individuals may elect, for a maximum period of five fiscal years, to be treated as transparent partnerships (régime des sociétés de personnes) subject to income tax at shareholder level. This election is filed with the competent tax authority and is irrevocable for the five-year period. Hybrid mismatch elections are limited and generally not available for domestic French entities; France applies the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) hybrid mismatch rules in domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold for foreign suppliers; anyone making taxable supplies of goods or services in France in the course of business must register for French VAT regardless of turnover. For distance sales of goods imported from other EU member states, an annual threshold of €10,000 applies for cross-border EU distance sales; beyond this, French VAT registration or OSS (One Stop Shop) registration is required. For non-EU suppliers, registration is required immediately upon the first taxable supply with no de minimis threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates electronic invoicing (e-invoicing) for B2B transactions between taxable persons established in France starting 1 September 2026, with mandatory e-reporting of transaction data to the DGFiP through the public portal (Portail Public de Facturation) or a certified private dematerialization platform (PDP). Invoicing data must be transmitted in structured electronic format (Factur-X). For B2C cross-border supplies, e-reporting is required. The system does not currently require real-time fiscal stamping or cryptographic seals, but data transmission is mandatory for all transactions subject to French VAT. For automated dropshipping platforms, integrated API-based reporting will be required to synchronize invoicing and transaction data with the prescribed dematerialization platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) applies to exports of goods physically shipped outside the European Union (Article 262 CGI) and to certain services directly related to exports such as transport. To claim zero-rating, the seller must prove that the goods were physically dispatched or transported outside the EU under the conditions of Article 262-0 CGI. The purchaser must be an economic operator, or the goods must be removed from EU customs territory. Evidence of removal is generally established within three months from the invoice date; the three-month deadline can be extended to one year upon prior request to the tax administration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane / Single Administrative Document - DAU),
Bill of Lading (Connaissement) or Air Waybill / CMR (international transport document),
Commercial invoice with mention of export nature, value and destination,
Inward Remittance Certificate / proof of payment from the foreign purchaser, where applicable, demonstrating actual receipt of consideration in euros or convertible currency, and
Proof of physical departure from EU customs territory (e.g., customs export stamp, electronic departure confirmation, or carrier certificate of shipment).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to stringent documentary scrutiny by the DGFiP. Failure to produce credible proof of export within the statutory deadline results in the reversal of the 0% rate and assessment of the standard VAT rate (20%) on the transaction along with interest for late payment (intérêts de retard). In cases of fictitious exports, fraudulent invoicing, or deliberate dissimulation, the tax administration may impose an 80% penalty for bad faith (manquement délibéré) or 100% for abusive manipulation or participation in a fraudulent scheme. Criminal sanctions may include fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment for the legal representatives under tax fraud provisions. Retrospective clawback can extend to all previously zero-rated exports of the same pattern within the statute of limitations period (generally three years, extended to six years for undisclosed facts).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is a fully convertible currency under the EU acquis and French law. Both current and capital accounts are liberalized with no prior authorization required for most transactions. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are permitted without restriction, subject only to standard beneficial ownership disclosure and post-transaction tax reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds is required under French law. Companies may retain foreign currency in offshore accounts. All export transactions must comply with French VAT (TVA) rules, be recorded in corporate accounts, and declared if exceeding reporting thresholds for customs or tax purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for regulated EU electronic money institutions such as Stripe and PayPal under French e-money and PSD2 frameworks. Direct cross-border EMI licensing for the SARL is prohibited; third-party platforms remain the only compliant channel for digital payment rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding via video KYC and e-ID verification is fully permitted for SARL directors and legal representatives. Physical presence is required only for initial high-value transactions exceeding €10,000 or specific regulatory triggers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of funds or inconsistent supplier payment volumes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier contracts, dropship confirmation records, VAT invoices, proof of goods receipt, and source-of-funds statements

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership not matching corporate filings
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Articles of association, shareholder register extracts, tax residency certificates, and updated beneficial ownership declarations

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from non-resident shareholders is routed via SWIFT wire transfer to the SARL French IBAN account using purpose code EQ. All injections require board resolutions and proof of shareholder identity. Transactions above €10,000 trigger enhanced due diligence and FX reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 messages with purpose codes such as SUPP for supplier payments. Commercial Letters of Credit are available for larger transactions through correspondent banks. All disbursements must reference underlying trade contracts and pass AML screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards for volatile currency exposure
Cross-currency swaps for multi-currency liquidity management
FX options for asymmetric risk protection

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (impôt sur les sociétés) for fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2022 (Article 219 CGI).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs (turnover < EUR 10m, capital fully paid up and ≥75% held by individuals or qualifying small entities). Social contribution of 3.3% on CIT applies only when annual CIT exceeds EUR 763,000. No sectoral holiday or tax credit applies to standardized automated dropshipping.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward (report en avant) with no statutory year cap; annual offset limited to EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding EUR 1,000,000 (Article 209 CGI, ATAD cap). Carry-back (report en arrière) abolished for deficits of fiscal years ending on or after 31 December 2021.
